title: The Four Faces of Light Sent from the Greatness and the Four Counterparts of Darkness
arc: From the Father of Greatness four operative Faces of Light go forth in ordered succession — First Man, Third Ambassador, Jesus the Radiance, and the Great Counsel — to descend into, redeem, and finally consume the cosmos; over against them stand four corresponding Faces of Darkness — King of Darkness, evil counsel, desire, and the law of Sin and Death — which mirror and oppose them at every level.
reading:
This teaching maps the whole drama of redemption onto a four-fold structure: four Faces of Light sent forth from the Father of Greatness, set against four Counterparts of Darkness that imitate and oppose them. (The chapter heading numbers it "5," but the Coptic text itself consistently reads "four faces" — ϩⲧⲁⲩ ⲛ̄ⲟⲉⲣϩⲟ — so the teaching unfolds as a fourfold parallel.) Each Face of Light is given the same anatomy: a "tree" (its characteristic perception or operative growth), a "stature" (the measure of its descent), a "ship" or "soul" (the vessel by which it carries truth), and a stated mission. The whole sequence describes how Divine Truth, proceeding from the inmost, "fulfills the purpose-of-heart of the Greatness" — the Lord's redemptive intention enacted through discrete operations into the depths of the natural and back again.

The **First Face is the First Man**, sent forth from the Greatness to guard the five storehouses (the five degrees of divine good held in form) and to "seize hold of the Enmity." This is Divine Truth in its initial descent: it goes down into the realm of self-love precisely to take hold of the principle of opposition. His tree, his stature, and his "four sons who ride upon his body" — read as the elemental Living Soul borne in his form — are the equipment of this first redemptive sortie. The sea is named here as the receptive natural depth into which he must enter.

The **Second Face is the Third Ambassador**. He acts "in his image" — the icon of light revealed forth into the abyss of the lower side — to send forth all the Light bound up in the works of the cosmos. His tree is precisely "his image of light," because the Ambassador's whole operation is to project the true likeness against which the darkness has taken souls captive ("she has taken them captive against this likeness"). His ship and his stature of light are the cosmos itself, used as the vessel and the field in which the awakening icon is displayed. This is the Lord's specific operation of awakening trapped good through revealed image.

The **Third Face is Jesus the Radiance**, who sends souls "to the Light and the Life" and "to the Height." Where the Ambassador reveals the saving icon below, Jesus raises what has been awakened. His tree is his Wisdom of light, which sends forth from herself unto the souls so that they may come up out of "the Error of the cosmos, the law of [death]" — the souls that lie suffering within it are gathered through his Wisdom of light. This is Divine Truth in its active redemptive shining, the upward complement to the Ambassador's downward unveiling.

The **Fourth Face is the Great Counsel** — the operative power of the Living Spirit, the cosmic builder and bearer. He "dwells in the encompassing-circuit" and contains the whole cosmos within himself "today"; but "at the end, in the dissolution of the cosmos," he draws all into himself alone. He is the depiction of the soul at the consummation. His soul is his living spirit, paired to the light and life dispersed in all works, having set them upon his body, with the wreath/crown of light fixed within him. From him proceeds the great fire that will burn all the constructions of darkness, releasing whatever is "perfected in his works" and binding the rest. He is therefore the eschatological Face: the one who gathers, judges, releases from bonds, and consigns the residue to the prepared great fire at the appointed times. Together the four Faces describe one continuous arc — descent (First Man), revelation in image (Ambassador), upward raising (Jesus), and final gathering-and-consummation (Great Counsel).

Against this fourfold operation stands a precise mirror in the realm of Darkness: **four living counterparts**, "counted to the Greatness" — that is, exactly numbered against the four Faces of Light, "from the Darkness." The **first** is the **King of Darkness**, paired to the Living Soul "in the beginning of the worlds": his soul is fire and desire — corrupt love and concupiscence — and he is the one set upon the soul to defile her with all his powers. He stands opposite the First Man, who came to seize the Enmity. The **second** is the **evil counsel**, who binds souls upward through the lands toward "the cosmos of the heaven of heavens," drawing them by his powers into false ascent — the dark mirror of the Ambassador's true revealing call. The **third** is **desire** itself, which grasps within every power of the flesh that lays hold of the living souls within its bodies — the inversion of Jesus's Wisdom that draws souls to the Height; here desire drags them into bodies. The **fourth** is the **law of Sin and Death which is king**, with its tree that casts souls down to death — the dark counterpart of the Great Counsel's tree that perfects souls and prepares the consummating fire. Where the Great Counsel ends in the great fire that releases the redeemed and binds the unredeemed, the law of Sin and Death is the legislative principle of that very downward casting which the consummation will at last reverse and seal.

The whole teaching is therefore a structural diagram of the cosmic conflict: the redemptive economy operates as four discrete acts of the one Divine Truth — descent, revelation, raising, and consummation — and at every stage the proprium has thrown up a counterpart — defilement, false ascent, fleshly grasp, and the law of death. To read the four Faces of Light is to see the whole work of regeneration laid out as a single fourfold movement; to read the four counterparts is to see why each phase of that movement is necessary, since each Face of Light comes precisely to undo the corresponding Face of Darkness. The teaching closes by anchoring the arc in the eschaton: the great fire prepared for the cosmos "at his times" is what the fourth Face will bring, completing the purpose-of-heart of the Greatness with which the teaching began.
